dedupe_keys.name: anatel open data licensed stations coverage quality indicators and sector statistics brazil

description: Anatel, Brazil's telecommunications regulator, publishes open datasets on the national open data portal under successive open data plans. Past and current plans cover licensed stations, including mobile base stations with technology and location, mobile coverage by municipality, operators' quality indicators under the service quality regulation (RQUAL), with quality seals and a Service Quality Index for mobile, fixed and broadband services, access counts, fines, consolidated economic indicators of the sector such as revenue, investment and costs, licensed VSAT satellite earth stations, and public regulatory texts. The plan for June 2025 to June 2027 adds datasets such as compensation proceedings and the agency's value chain. Data come as CSV spreadsheets with glossaries, published on dados.gov.br under an open licence that allows free use and combination, with update frequencies from monthly to half-yearly. Anatel's SMP station panel also lets users browse mobile stations. Coverage: Brazil, national, by operator and municipality, from about 2016 for most series. Format and access: CSV files and dictionaries from dados.gov.br and Anatel panels, free. Caveats: datasets are spread across the portal and some older series are only in the legacy portal; station coordinates can be approximate. Simulation uses: asset inventories of mobile networks, service performance baselines, coverage for exposure studies and economic inputs. Related records: OpenCelliD gives crowdsourced cell locations worldwide, and ANFR and ARCEP play the same role in France.
